summary: Wilde named Francesco to Robert Ross as one of the three most favoured of the Monreale coachmen, and said 'I loved them all'.

sources.quote: Monreale you have heard of, with its cloisters and cathedral. We often drove there, the cocchieri most dainty finely-carved boys. In them, not in the Sicilian horses, is race seen. The most favoured were Manuele, Francesco, and Salvatore. I loved them all, but only remember Manuele.
sources.context: Wilde to Robert Ross, 16 April [1900], c/o Cook & Son, Piazza di Spagna, Rome (MS Clark), quoted across the page break. 'cocchieri' are coachmen. Wilde had spent eight days at Palermo and drove out to Monreale repeatedly. Seven months before his death.
sources.speaker: Oscar Wilde
sources.supports: The whole of the record for Francesco.

manuscript.repository: William Andrews Clark Memorial Library, UCLA
